title: Atletico Madrid vs. Man Utd: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 12, 2026Atlético and Manchester United are in contrasting form heading into the game.  / Alex Caparros/UEFA/Getty Images (Atlético’s badge), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Man Utd’s badge) Manchester United’s Champions League league phase campaign restarts with a tough test away at Atlético Madrid.

Michael Carrick inspired the Red Devils back into Europe’s premier club competition after his appointment as interim manager in January, but the now-full-time boss hasn’t enjoyed the added challenges at the start of the 2026–27 campaign.

United were deservedly pegged back by the 10 men of Tottenham Hotspur at the weekend, extending their winless run in domestic competitions to four matches. Carrick’s side are currently plagued by distinct issues without possession, and while running statistics aren’t the be-all and end-all, United are unlikely to win many matches playing with the intensity they’ve offered in recent outings.
A switch of environment could benefit the under-fire Red Devils, even if few enjoy their trips to the Metropolitano.

Atlético enter this bout having won each of their previous four games, and one of their notable summer arrivals, Cristian Romero, was the match-winner at the weekend. Romero’s 88th-minute goal fired Atléti past Alavés on Saturday, keeping Diego Simeone’s side above cross-city rivals Real Madrid in the La Liga table.

Carrick is feeling the heat. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesMan Utd at least got their Champions League campaign up and running on their first attempt, easing past debutants Sabah 4–0. Atlético Madrid, meanwhile, were beaten 2–1 at Anfield.

While United have appeared ever so easy to play against on either side of the extended break, this competition may suit Carrick’s side. On Tuesday, there will be less onus on Carrick’s side to assert control, and they’ll be happy to play on the counterattack, even in Benjamin Šeško’s absence.

Ultimately, United have generally been most successful over the past decade when they’ve played a transitional game. Thus, the opening goal feels crucial in the Spanish capital, given Atléti’s own counterattacking threat.

You never quite know what you’re going to get from Simeone’s side nowadays, but the Argentine will hope that the summer arrival of Romero and continued development of Marc Pubill will help shore up a defense that was leaky last season.
/    Simeone is set to have a full cohort of players available for Man Utd‘s visit. The Argentine must thus decided upon the correct configuration.

They’ve switched between a back three and four at the start of the new season, with a 4-2-3-1 installed against Alavés at the weekend. That could be retained here, with Álex Baena operating behind Alvarez as the No. 10.

Simeone has Alexander Sørloth to call upon in reserve, as well as Jonathan David, if Alvarez’s quiet start to the campaign continues. Kang-in Lee and Ademola Lookman offer dynamic threats out wide, and Koke is still going strong in midfield alongside the excellent Pablo Barrios.
Romero was sent off on his previous encounter against the Red Devils earlier this year, and he’ll lead Atléti’s improved defense on Tuesday.
Atlético Madrid predicted lineup vs. Man Utd (4-2-3-1): Oblak; Llorente, Romero, Pubill, Hancko; Koke, Barrios; Lee, Baena, Lookman; Alvarez.
Man Utd have been dealt a couple of fresh injury blows heading into Tuesday’s league phase clash.

Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo didn’t train with the rest of the team on Monday, throwing their availability for the match into doubt. As it stands, it seems unlikely for either to feature, given the quick turnaround and their respective injury histories. Mainoo, of course, withdrew from Thomas Tuchel’s England roster due to a fitness concern.

Carrick will have to reshuffle his defense as a result of poor depth at left back in Shaw’s absence. Diogo Dalot could come across to the opposite flank, allowing Leny Yoro to keep his place at right back.

Carlos Baleba is almost assured of a first Man Utd start after impressing off the bench against Spurs on his debut. Youri Tielemans may partner his fellow new arrival, despite his struggles at the weekend.
The visitors are also still without Patrick Dorgu, Benjamin Šeško and Noussair Mazraoui.
